title: An aggregate app in front of members
lede: Many MCP servers sit behind one address; the prefixed grant on the aggregate decides which tools a caller sees, and each member's own policy still applies.

steps.title: One address for many servers
steps.what: An MCP Aggregate application has a name that becomes its address and a list of member MCP Server apps; it has no backend or Auth Mode of its own.
steps.why: Each tool is listed as member alias, two underscores, tool name.

steps.title: The prefixed grant decides
steps.what: The grant on the aggregate, written in prefixed form, decides which tools the caller sees and can call.
steps.why: When a call arrives the aggregate strips the prefix and opens a session to that member as the calling user.

steps.title: Refusals look like success
steps.what: In testing, refusals came back as JSON-RPC errors with HTTP 200 rather than the bare 403 of a plain MCP Server app.
steps.why: A client that checks only the HTTP status could read them as success; the wording varied.
